notes: Unfilled on purpose, blocked by network, not by absence of a service. The Secretary of the State's expedited-service document lives on business.ct.gov, and that host — like portal.ct.gov — establishes no TCP connection from this machine on either network route, with DNS pinned to its public addresses included; the same is true of the retired CONCORD hosts. The statutes the state does publish reachably were read in full: the Uniform LLC Act (chapter 613a) contains no occurrence of 'expedit' at all, and chapter 601's only 'expedited' language is about court procedure, so the expedite fee is administrative rather than statutory and only the unreachable host states it. service.ct.gov answers and titles itself 'Connecticut Business', but it is a client-rendered application that serves no quotable text to a scripted client. Nothing is recorded rather than anything guessed.
needsReview: Every expedite field and the standard-processing fields. Two follow-ups, both for a browser session: (1) service.ct.gov/s/ renders in a real browser and may carry the expedited-service content that used to live on business.ct.gov — read it there and verify against a saved snapshot; (2) if it names a fee document, fetch that document from whatever host serves it. business.ct.gov itself is closed as a network matter from this machine — do not re-probe it.

sources.title: General Statutes chapter 613a (Uniform Limited Liability Company Act) — consulted in full; contains no expedited-service provision
General Statutes chapter 601 (Business Corporations) — consulted; 'expedited' occurs only in court-procedure provisions, no service fee
